title: session-aware-entitlement-design-and-evidence-automation-draft
body:
Purpose:
- Capture design notes for a session-bound RBAC extension and an evidence automation pipeline that produces SIEM-ready export artifacts.
- Focus is on minimizing noise in export events and preserving ephemeral delegation context for forensic queries.

Background / Motivation:
- RBAC v2 currently models static permission bindings on principals and groups. Many product flows create short-lived delegation (e.g., console impersonation, cross-service proxy tokens, ephemeral session roles).
- Existing audit events often lose session context (session_id, parent_delegation_id, auth_method) which makes forensic reconstruction hard and inflates SIEM storage with correlated repetitive events.

High-level goals:
1) Add session-scoped entitlement objects that can be referenced by runtime checks and included in audit evidence.
2) Produce an evidence automation pipeline that deduplicates and enriches raw events into compact SIEM exports with pointers to retained artifacts.
3) Allow safe fast-rollout: start as opt-in shadow-mode and provide visible KPIs to product owners.

Key concepts / data model (informal):
- session_id: opaque UUID created at authentication or impersonation start.
- session_claims: list of derived entitlements active for the session (strings like: scope:read:workspace-42, temporary:role:readonly@2026-02-01T10:04Z).
- delegation_chain: ordered list of actor IDs and delegation reasons (max depth 8, persisted as compressed string).
- policy_fingerprint: a deterministic hash of the effective permission set used at decision time. Useful for comparing audits across time.
- evidence_pointer: opaque reference to the archived full event payload in the evidence store (S3/GCS). SIEM export includes pointer, not full payload.

Example audit event (single-line JSON for SIEM export):
{
  "ts":"2026-02-18T14:21:05Z",
  "principal":"user:jordan.kim",
  "session_id":"sess-0a4f7e9c",
  "action":"deploy:model.start",
  "resource":"model:prod-bert-embedding",
  "decision":"allow",
  "policy_fingerprint":"f2b9c1e7",
  "delegation_abbrev":"svc:hc-proxy->user:ops-oncall",
  "evidence_ptr":"s3://evidence-prod/2026/02/18/evt-12345.gz"
}

Design notes:
- Audit production should emit two tiers of events: lightweight SIEM-friendly rows (above) and verbose archival events. SIEM rows are small and indexed, verbose events go to cold storage.
- During check-time, runtime attaches session_id and policy_fingerprint to every authorization decision event.
- Policy fingerprint computed via canonical serialization of effective grants + dynamic constraints (time, region) then sha1. Store mapping in a compact metadata table to translate fingerprint->grant-set when needed.
- To reduce churn, run a daily fingerprint compaction job: fast compare, aliasing similar fingerprints to a dominant representative.
- Delegation chain must be truncated but include hints for first-hop and last-hop for quick triage. Full chain available from evidence store.

Evidence automation pipeline (sketch):
1) Event ingestion (kinesis/pubsub) receives decision events with full context.
2) Stream enrichment stage: resolve principal display names, map resource tags, compute policy_fingerprint if missing.
3) Dedup and collapse stage: within a sliding window (default 30s) collapse repetitive identical decisions for same session_id+resource+action into a single summarized row with count and time-range.
4) Export writer: sends compact rows to SIEM ingest (via connector) and archives verbose payloads to evidence-store.
5) Backfill worker: samples historical compact rows and cross-checks with archived verbose payloads to validate fidelity.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: Feature flags and runtime hooks (engineering spike). Enable session_id emission behind flag. Run no-op.
- Phase 1: Shadow mode (30 days): emit compact SIEM rows to a non-production SIEM index for analysis. Collate KPIs: event collapse ratio, sessions with delegation, fingerprint cardinality.
- Phase 2: Opt-in prod export: selected teams opt in to full SIEM export. Start archiving verbose events for opt-in tenants.
- Phase 3: Global opt-out default: flip to opt-out with strict retention defaults and tenant controls.

Validation & KPIs to monitor during rollout:
- event_collapse_ratio = (raw_events / exported_rows) target >= 8x
- delegation_traceability_score = percent of incidents where session + delegation_chain recreate root cause target >= 95%
- policy_fingerprint_cardinality = number of distinct fingerprints per 1M decisions (monitor for explosion)
- SIEM_cost_delta = delta in ingestion storage vs prior baseline

Migration checklist (practical):
- Update SDKs and internal auth libraries to accept and propagate session_id.
- Instrument all major service runtimes to include session_claims in decisions.
- Create policy_fingerprint registry table with TTL index.
- Implement dedup/collapse step and validate summarization with product owners.
- Add an evidence retention policy and lifecycle jobs for archival pointers referenced in SIEM.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle privacy-sensitive session claims (PII) when included in fingerprints or short SIEM rows? Mask before export?
- Potential for fingerprint churn creating storage blowup; need heuristics for aliasing similar fingerprints without losing forensic fidelity.
- Performance impact of computing policy_fingerprint on hot paths. Consider asynchronous compute for non-blocking requests.
- Cross-region session continuity: if session moves across region, ensure session_id global uniqueness and export routing consistent.

Operational runbooks (notes):
- SIEM alerting: new rule templates for sudden increase in delegation_abbrev variants.
- Forensics: provide a tool that accepts session_id and fetches compact SIEM rows + archived verbose events, reconstructing timeline.
- Incident triage play: if delegation_abbrev not present, check last auth event for session and fall back to archived chain.

Appendix: quick PoC tasks:
- PoC A: instrument one internal service (console proxy) to emit session_id + simple policy_fingerprint. Generate 7 days of shadow exports.
- PoC B: implement the dedup/collapse lambda and measure collapse ratio on PoC data.
- PoC C: run privacy review on session_claims and define allowed claim patterns.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working-draft with design trade-offs surfaced. Please annotate with comments on Confluence (linked above) or drop thoughts on #sec-rbac thread.

Unresolved action items:
- [ ] Decide canonical hashing algorithm for policy_fingerprint (sha1 vs blake2b).
- [ ] Define exact compression format for delegation_chain (gzip vs snappy).
- [ ] Finalize retention policy for archived verbose events (default 365 days?).

Last edited by Jordan Kim on 2026-02-18.
